name: Tiranige
catalog_citation: Heath, Jeffrey. 2022. A grammar of Tiranige (Dogon, Mali). Language Description Heritage Library / Zenodo record 6350672 (PDF 'Heath Tiranige grammar 2022 B&W', 444 pp.).
catalog_locator: sec. 3.5 Cliticization, p. 33 (PDF p. 48); sec. 3.6 Tones, p. 34 (PDF p. 49); sec. 3.1.2 Metrical structure, p. 15 (PDF p. 30)
catalog_quote: [3.5] There are no second-position clitics of the Wackernagel type. The extent to which we should recognize phonological clitics is debatable. There are many function elements, often monosyllabic or subsyllabic, that could be considered as affixes, clitics, or particles (or, in verb complexes, auxiliaries). ... There is no stress or accent system that would clearly distinguish affixes, clitics, and particles. ... [3.6] Individual syllables are usually L or H, but contour-toned syllables <HL> and <LH> also occur in monosyllabics and in word-final syllables. <LHL> is rare ... There are no <HLH> syllables. ... [3.6.1.1] In nouns and numerals, and to a lesser extent adjectives, stems have a lexical tone melody. Tiranige belongs to the subset of Dogon languages that allow lexically /L/-toned stems. In other words, there is no requirement that all stems have at least one H-tone. ... [3.1.2] I…

audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: The 'tonal' (no stress/accent system) coding rests on the sole and current reference grammar (Heath 2022, 444 pp.), which we hold; the deciding sentence and the supporting tone and metrical-structure passages are verbatim at the stated pages (p. 33/PDF 48, p. 34/PDF 49, p. 15/PDF 30). Heath explicitly says there is no stress or accent system and describes syllable-level H/L/contour tones with lexical melodies and grammatical overlays; the only 'metrical' remark (weak medial syllable in CvCvCv conditioning raising/syncope) is already captured in the record's the secondary-stress rule and does not amount to a stress rule. Glottolog lists no other descriptive works and Zenodo shows no newer version or separate phonology study, so nothing available would change the classification. No works still to obtain.
